meta.title: Journal finder
meta.description: Match your paper to open access journals, institutional deals, and funder policies using local semantic search.

header.heading: Find an open access journal for your paper
header.intro: Answer four questions about your paper, funder, and budget. We match your text locally against {institution} publishing deals, open access models, and journal topics.

manuscript.heading: Describe your paper
manuscript.description: Paste a working title and abstract, or write a short summary of your study. We compare your text with journal scopes and recent articles.
manuscript.titlePlaceholder: e.g. Droplet formation dynamics in microfluidic T-junctions
manuscript.abstractPlaceholder: Paste your abstract, methods, or a few sentences about your study...
manuscript.charCountNeeded: Add at least {remaining} more characters across the title and abstract.

microfluidics.title: Interfacial dynamics and breakup regimes of viscoelastic droplets in microfluidic T-junctions
microfluidics.abstract: We investigate the formation and pinch-off dynamics of viscoelastic polymer droplets in planar microfluidic T-junction channels using high-speed optical imaging and particle image velocimetry. By varying the capillary number, flow rate ratio, and fluid elasticity, we map transitions between squeezing, dripping, and jetting regimes and derive a scaling law for droplet volume control in lab-on-a-chip synthesis.

membranes.title: Polyelectrolyte multilayer nanofiltration membranes for selective micropollutant removal in wastewater reuse
membranes.abstract: Hollow-fiber nanofiltration membranes fabricated via layer-by-layer assembly of polyelectrolytes are evaluated for high-recovery municipal wastewater reclamation. We measure permeance, monovalent versus divalent ion selectivity, and retention of pharmaceutical micropollutants under cross-flow fouling conditions, demonstrating chemical cleaning stability over extended filtration cycles.

responsibleAi.title: Auditing algorithmic fairness and transparency in public-sector automated decision systems
responsibleAi.abstract: Public administrations increasingly deploy machine learning models for risk assessment and resource allocation, raising legal and ethical concerns around accountability and disparate impact. We combine socio-technical impact assessments with empirical fairness audits under the EU AI Act to propose a participatory governance framework for trustworthy public-sector AI.

manuscript.privacyBody: Your text is converted to a vector on this server. We do not store it, log it, or send it to any external service.

funder.heading: Does your research funder have open access rules?
funder.description: If you select a funder, we check each candidate journal against its Jisc Open Policy Finder record and save that choice in your browser.
funder.yesDesc: Check journals against NWO, Horizon Europe, ERC, ZonMw, or any funder listed in Jisc Open Policy Finder.
funder.noDesc: Prioritize diamond open access and {institution} publishing deals without a separate funder check.
funder.selectPrompt: Pick a funder above or search below to check its policy. You can also continue without selecting one.

budget.heading: What is your publishing (APC) budget?
budget.description: Diamond open access journals and active {institution} publishing deals always rank ahead of paid options.
budget.noneDesc: Show only €0 options, namely diamond open access journals and active {institution} publishing deals.
budget.cappedDesc: Include gold open access journals up to a maximum fee, alongside €0 diamond open access and institutional deals.
budget.funderPaysTitle: Funder or grant covers the APC
budget.funderPaysDesc: Show all open access journals eligible for grant reimbursement. Diamond journals and institutional deals still rank first.
budget.anyDesc: Include all topically relevant journals, including subscription journals, and label their open access options.
budget.capCustomHint: Or enter an amount in euros from 0 to 50,000.

preferences.heading: Optional ranking settings
preferences.description: Topic similarity always remains the main ranking factor. You can turn any of these extra weights on or off.
preferences.historyDesc: Adds a small score bonus for journals that already have recent {institution} publications.
preferences.establishedDesc: Adds a small score bonus for Scimago Q1 and Q2 journals. Following DORA, use journal indicators as context rather than a measure of article quality.
preferences.nonJournalsTitle: Include conference series and book series
preferences.nonJournalsDesc: Include book series and proceedings series such as Lecture Notes in Computer Science alongside peer-reviewed journals.

results.heading: Recommended journals
results.subheading: Ranked from {pool} topically similar venues, with {strict} {strict, plural, one {exact match} other {exact matches}} for your filters.
results.moreMatchesIntro: Other journals that meet all of your selected rules.
results.alternativesIntro: Fewer than three journals met every filter. The venues below are close to your topic and show which requirement would need to change, such as using green open access or paying a higher APC.
results.noResultsBody: Add a few more domain terms or sentences to your summary, or loosen your budget and venue filters.
results.transparencyLead: The server encodes your text locally with the bge-small-en-v1.5 model, compares it with journal embeddings in PostgreSQL, and ranks candidates using the fixed rules below.
